overview: Great Zimbabwe was a stone-built center created by ancestors of the Shona. Its surviving walls preserve part of a larger settlement of homes, courtyards and monumental enclosures.

items.text: Builders fitted local granite slabs together without mortar. Successive courses stepped inward, giving the curving walls a stabilizing inward slope.
Eight surviving soapstone bird sculptures combine human and bird features. Their precise meaning remains uncertain; an association with royal authority is one interpretation.
Stone walls stood beside homes made from daga, a building material of earth, with thatched roofs. Painted surfaces and enclosed courtyards formed parts of the lived settlement.

sources.title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Great Zimbabwe (11th to 15th century)
sources.note: Department of the Arts of Africa, Oceania, and the Americas, 2001. See the discussions of masonry, bird sculptures and daga buildings.
